findings.refactoring: Extract Function / Move Function onto the scope token (or a small shared helper) so the rule 'under AWAIT_ALL, once every member settles with at least one failure, commit fail-fast to cancel the never-submitted terminal combine' has one owner
rationales: The same rule is written twice with different member-settle tracking: TaskGroup#skipCombineAfterAllMembersSettled counts settledMembers per completion and compares memberSuccesses, while Par#executeCombined's onFailure callback builds a second Futures.successfulAsList(views) aggregate and fires unit.cancellationToken().failFastCancel() from its listener. Both then rely on failFastCancel() to cancel a combine that was bound but never submitted, producing ABORTED_BY_FAIL_FAST. Centralizing the rule (e.g. a package-private CancellationToken method fed by each caller's member-settle signal) makes the skip timing, the failure gate, and the ABORTED_BY_FAIL_FAST attribution change in exactly one place instead of two protocol implementations.
behaviorRisks: Must keep the settling thread committing FAIL_FAST before the convergence barrier counts the terminal combine; the terminal must still read ABORTED_BY_FAIL_FAST and never run; the all-success submit path and the FAIL_FAST path (where the token's own aggregate already cancels the combine) must stay untouched; deadline, cancelOn, and parent cancellation must still cancel every unfinished member.

rationales: failedTask() is documented to run only at convergence, when every member and combine termination is already recorded, so the `termination != null` guard can never be false. Treating the impossible null as "not failed" silently masks a broken invariant and could let the group report success or a wrong cancellation; the neighboring code (memberSnapshot, freezeValues) states this same invariant with `Verify.verifyNotNull(member.termination, "member termination is recorded before convergence")`. Replacing the guard with that Verify makes the invariant explicit, fail-fast, and consistent with the Guava conditional-failure taxonomy.
behaviorRisks: None on reachable paths: convergence guarantees a non-null termination for every member and the combine, so the Verify never fires in any state the tests can reach.

findings.refactoring: Move Comment (Javadoc → block comment): keep only the behavioral contract in Javadoc and move the ordering/race proof beside the statements it justifies
rationales: The Javadoc's second half ('Called by each member's completion after its own success count is published, so the thread that settles the last member sees every member's count; the cascade completes the combine, whose own completion runs nested on this thread before the calling member is counted by the convergence barrier') is a maintainer-only ordering/race proof. ADR 0012 and the conventions require such proofs in ordinary block comments next to the statements, not in Javadoc; moving it makes the proof reviewable against the exact statements it guards while the Javadoc keeps only the callable contract.

findings.refactoring: Move Comment (Javadoc → block comment): keep the frozen-data/orThrow contract in Javadoc and move the precedence enumeration into an ordinary in-method comment
rationales: The 'in this order: first FAILED element ... first cancelled element' enumeration is a maintainer-only local protocol (the derivation algorithm), while the final sentence ('depends only on frozen data, never on settlement order, so it names the same failure orThrow() throws') is the contract a reader relies on. Per ADR 0012 and the conventions, the algorithm belongs in an ordinary block comment inside the private method, leaving Javadoc to state only the contract.

everyMemberSucceedingStillRunsTheCombine, theLastMemberFailureCancelsTheCombineBeforeConvergence, and aSuccessfulLastMemberAfterAnEarlierFailureStillCancelsTheCombine each rebuild the identical scaffold — a ParRuntime registering a direct executor, two SettableFuture members adopted into an AWAIT_ALL group draft, and a combine submitted with submitAll — differing only in the group name and the combine lambda. A private helper that takes the name and combine function and returns the futures plus the submitted group would make the combine-cancellation setup a single point of change, leaving each test to state only its settle order and assertions.
behaviorRisks: none; each test keeps its own settle order, combine lambda, and literal assertion values, and no test input or timing changes.
